action: Limit internet-connected devices and systems and use multi-factor authentication, as the NCSC advises.
date_note: 1News's article is dated 22 November in New Zealand (21 November UTC); that publication day is used as the source gives no other date.
exec: New Zealand's cyber agency says attackers can now automate attack stages with an AI tool, cutting the time from reconnaissance to exploitation.
plain: New Zealand's cyber security agency warns that attackers are using an open source AI tool, copies of which exist after it was taken down, to speed up attacks on organisations.
summary: 1News reports that Dr Emma Bickerstaffe of New Zealand's National Cyber Security Centre said attackers have used the open source AI tool Artex against organisations worldwide over the past week. She said it was built by researchers, taken down, then copied, and lets attackers automate attacks on several organisations at once. She said some attempts in New Zealand failed and others gained access and viewed data.
title: NZ cyber agency warns attackers are using open source AI tool Artex against organisations

validation.note: Only 1News's report of the NCSC statement was read; the NCSC's own page was not found.
